findings.claim: Client-to-route HTTP edges extract exactly. All 75 production URL literal sites (mobile and web) match a backend or ops-server route by method and path. All 380 backend test HTTP calls match too.
findings.detail: Done with the TypeScript 5.3.3 compiler API from technician-app plus the Python ast module. A ${...} placeholder after a slash becomes {}; other placeholders and ?... are treated as the query and dropped. The HTTP method comes from the options {method} or the apiSend second argument. When two routes match, the one with more literal segments wins. Result: 0 ambiguous matches and 4 non-literal wrapper calls; the wrapper's inner literal is still captured. 53 of 77 backend routes have a client; 24 have none (ledger, advances, shop settings, webhooks, health, ops). 73 routes are exercised over HTTP by pytest. These edges are invisible to an import graph and to plain grep.
findings.source: measured: ts_extract.js, py_extract.py, join.js in the lane folder

findings.claim: Python function-level calls resolve at about 98.5% recall for in-repo targets using stdlib ast and lightweight type rules. Precision was 25 of 25 in a sample.
findings.detail:
8,335 call sites. 2,377 resolve to in-repo definitions (2,085 distinct edges), 3,786 are external, 2,034 name no repo definition. Only 36 sites whose name matches a repo definition stay unresolved: callbacks (dead_letter, handler, on_orphan), module singletons (metrics_registry), chained constructors and local closures. Typing rules that made the difference:
- imports and re-exports
- self methods, including base classes
- __init__ attribute types
- Annotated[...] dependency aliases followed across modules
- pytest fixture return types, including tuple[JobService, MagicMock] unpacking: fixed 256 test calls (680 unresolved before)
- closure scope: fixed build_dispatch_handler.handle -> JobService.log_customer_message, which is the exact edge a CLAUDE.md invariant names
- return annotations of called methods
Backend extraction takes 0.7 to 1.35 s.

findings.claim: TypeScript and JavaScript calls resolve through the compiler's type checker with 20 of 20 precision in a sample. The remaining dynamic calls are React context and prop callbacks.
findings.detail: 2,358 resolved in-repo call sites; 1,259 are production code, giving 946 distinct production pairs (mobile 814 sites, web 445). Unresolved production calls are mostly built-ins on untyped JS values (web 231). Unresolved test calls are jest globals (2,229), because @types/jest is not in the program. Not resolved: about 32 production calls to functions destructured from context (useApp, useAuth) and 37 on* prop callbacks. JSX renders of in-repo components: mobile 40 of 968 elements, web 336 of 1,448. Both programs build in 2.6 to 2.75 s.

findings.claim: Table-level edges need unit-of-work detection. Without it, 8 mutating routes appear to write no table; with it, 1 does.
findings.detail: Write edges come from four sources. ORM select/update/insert/delete(Model): 125 production. Model(...) constructors: 46 production. Raw SQL inside text(): 23 production. Unit of work, i.e. assigning an attribute on a variable typed from a method's return annotation (tech = await self._load(); tech.pin_hash = ...; flush): 98 production. That last source also yields writes_column (190 sites, 175 distinct). A 16-edge sample of table edges was all correct. The one remaining miss is session.delete(obj) on the DELETE media route. Test-file constructor and unit-of-work edges (161) are not database writes and must be dropped.

findings.claim: Hop count matters only for hubs and for cross-runtime questions. A single global hop limit is wrong either way; the budget should be set per edge type (a metapath).
findings.detail:
Reverse reach over 507 production backend functions, tests excluded:
- median 1/2/3/4/6 at hops 1/2/3/4/6
- p90 3/8/15/22/34
- max 52/129/200/259/320, all from core.db:get_session
A change to JobService.submit_completion needs 8 hops to reach the mobile screens: handler, route, client function, outbox kind, enqueue sites. A depth-2 limit stops at the route. Of 33 cross-runtime co-change pairs (support of 3 or more commits), the typed graph joins them at distance 2 (2 pairs), 3 (7), 4 (13) and 5 (8); 3 are not joined within 8 hops.

findings.claim: Hubs flood answers in three distinct ways here, and each needs its own damping. Plain degree cut-offs fail.
findings.detail:
(1) String-dispatch hub: outboxSync.ts send switches over all 10 outbox kinds. Forward from ArrivalJobBillScreen over call edges reaches 14 routes; over kind edges (enqueue site -> kind -> jobsApi method) it reaches 8. That is 6 false routes, 43%.
(2) Test-inflated degree: a stop rule of degree over 15 counting all edges cut the impact answer for submit_completion from 28 nodes to 2, because routes carry 380 test edges. Degree must be computed on production edges per edge type. With production in-degree over 10 the answer is 15 nodes.
(3) Infrastructure providers: get_session has 52 direct dependency-injection dependants and reaches 320 nodes in 6 hops. A degree stop of over 5 still leaves 221, because each dependant has a low degree. Other transport hubs: api.ts request (38 callers, 113 nodes reached), apiGet (24), useApp (16). Fix: tag these as infrastructure and exclude them from impact queries, and attach URL edges at the API function (jobsApi.claim) rather than at the transport.

findings.claim: Test reach needs route edges plus an overrides edge; call edges alone miss most integration tests and naive route edges add false positives.
findings.detail:
Tests reaching JobService.submit_completion:
- 23 at hop 1 by direct call
- 16 at hop 3 via test -> route -> handler -> service, plus 3 more at hops 4 to 6
- 13 integration tests reach it only over HTTP
- 3 router tests in test_router.py appear to reach it, but they override get_jobs_service with an AsyncMock, so they are false positives

recommendations_for_the_build: Use typed edges with a hop budget per edge type (metapaths), not one global hop limit. Example: calls up to 3 within a runtime, then exactly one calls_url hop, one registers_route hop, calls up to 3 on the backend, then one writes_table hop.

Extract in this order of value for effort:
(1) route table + client URL matching + pytest HTTP calls
(2) Python calls with the measured type rules (imports/re-exports, self and bases, __init__ attributes, Annotated Depends aliases, pytest fixture return types including tuple unpacking, closure scope, return annotations) + Depends + passes_callable
(3) tables, columns and FKs; reads and writes including unit-of-work attribute writes; migration chain and touches; settings
(4) outbox kind and navigation-name edges
(5) TS/JS calls and JSX renders through the TypeScript compiler API
(6) test dependency_overrides and fixture scope
(7) CLAUDE.md invariants and the document graph
(8) git co-change as a ranking signal
(9) context and prop callback resolution
Route the outbox through kind nodes (enqueue site -> kind -> jobsApi method) and never through the outboxSync send switch. Measured: the switch adds 6 false routes out of 14.

Compute hub degree per edge type on production edges only. Tag transport and infrastructure providers (core.db get_session, api.ts request, apiGet/apiSend, useApp, makeItem/sendOrQueue) and exclude them from impact paths unless asked.
Attach calls_url edges at the enclosing API function (for example jobsApi.claim), not at the transport function.
Add an overrides edge from test files that set app.dependency_overrides[provider]. Cut test-reach paths through an overridden provider. Label each test as unit, router-with-fakes or integration.
Drop constructor and unit-of-work table edges that come from test files. Handle session.delete(obj). Keep raw-SQL table references with via=sql.

Key document ids as (doc family, id). Add version/supersede links between family members. Give each citation edge a resolved, ambiguous or not-in-repo status. Index untracked docs and code, because 45 of 83 md files under docs/ are untracked.

Make tables, columns, UPPER constants, config keys and import-linter contract edges first-class nodes and edges, so invariants can anchor to them. With those types 18 of 19 anchor; with files and symbols only, 16 of 19.
Rebuild per worktree at query time (about 5 s full). Make the Python stage incremental per file. The TS stage needs the whole program, about 2.6 s, unless an incremental builder is used.
Return answers ranked and grouped by slice, runtime and test/prod within a token budget. A raw transitive list floods on hub targets.
recommendations_for_the_test: Score answers on correctness and completeness against hand-checked ground truth, not on size. Measured examples of where structure changes the answer: kind-aware vs call-only routes from a screen (8 vs 14 routes); test reach with and without route and override edges (13 integration tests missed by call edges; 3 false via mocked routers).

Use repo-specific question sets with known hop requirements:
- screen -> tables (7-9 hops)
- service impact across runtimes (up to 8)
- tests reaching a function (1-6)
- invariants on a file (1-2)
- other half of a rule (2-3)
- setting readers (1-3)
- migrations touching a table

Give the relational baseline the same typed edges and the same hop budgets: SQLite recursive CTEs with an edge-type filter per step. The comparison should test the store and the algorithms, not the extraction.
Vary the hop limit per question type and report the answer size in tokens at each hop. Reverse reach p90 grows 3/8/15/22/34 over hops 1/2/3/4/6, and the maximum reaches 320 at hop 6.
Include hub-heavy targets (get_session, api.ts request, sendOrQueue) and ordinary targets. Report damping variants: none, production in-degree, edge-type exclusion, ranking.
Use the co-change pairs at support 3 or more (387) as a weak external check of 'what changes together'. The typed graph joins 30 of 33 cross-runtime pairs within 5 hops.

findings.claim: Agent Retrieval Bench gives a ready token-budgeted metric (BCY@B) and change-evidence gold labels that match this repo's task types.
findings.detail:
BCY@B packing: ranked files are packed greedily, each as a path header plus content; the last file is cut at the budget, and headers count against the budget.
- A gold file counts as exposed if at least 1 content token is visible.
- Tokens are counted with a deterministic regex code tokenizer.
- Budgets are 4k to 32k, with 8k as the main point.

Gold labels come from change evidence (code2test, edit2ripple, trace2code). The corpus is frozen at the pre-fix base commit, and queries exclude patches and gold paths.

Result: no retrieval family dominates; RepoMap is best at 8k.

Bowyer et al. (ICML 2025 position paper) find that CLT intervals dramatically underestimate uncertainty below a few hundred datapoints.

recommendations_for_the_build:
Use one shared extractor that writes a single typed node/edge set loaded into both stores, so the comparison tests storage and queries, not extraction quality.
- Nodes: file, symbol, route, table, doc section.
- Edges: contain, import, call, HTTP route linking client to backend, tested-by, migration-to-model, doc-cites, and co-change from ancestor commits with time decay.

Store spans at symbol granularity (file, start line, end line), so either arm can return only the changed definition instead of whole files. Granularity is how 'the data structure changes the answer' gets measured under a token budget.

Make co-change an available edge type in both stores. On its own it reaches recall@10 of about 0.54 here. A graph without it competes against a stronger relational table, which is an unfair comparison.

Invest in typed cross-runtime edges (client URL literal to route decorator). Cross-runtime tasks are where the baselines are weakest (COxPR@10 0.335), so that is where a graph's typed traversal could show value.
Build the graph arm as a hybrid of text search and graph traversal, not traversal alone. In LocAgent's ablation, removing text search cost about 18 points and removing traversal about 5.
Every answer should carry a frontier or unresolved list, so an empty result is never read as 'no dependency' (A6-06).

Implement the same retrieval designs (k-hop typed BFS, PPR, hybrid BM25-then-graph) in both engines as arm (d). Their ranked outputs must be identical; if they are not, that is a bug to fix before scoring.
recommendations_for_the_test:
Run these steps as scripts at zero model tokens:
1. Freeze main at a31924a and the split date at 2026-07-01, and hash the config.
2. Build T1, T1x and T2 from task_pool_commits.py. Get symbol references from git diff -U0 hunks mapped to their enclosing definitions at the parent (Python ast; the TypeScript compiler from technician-app/node_modules). Build T3 and T6 from doc_chains.json and doc_symbols.json, and T4 from the register-to-fix map.
3. Seal tasks.jsonl and references.jsonl with SHA-256; the build scripts get no read access to them.
4. For each parent: git archive it, extract the facts, cache them by SHA, and log every path read.
5. Load the facts into the relational and graph arms; implement arm (a) and the (d) designs.
6. Run the sweep on the tune split under an equal configuration budget per arm. Pick by M1 with the parsimony rule (simplest configuration within 1 standard error of the best), then freeze the configuration hash.
7. Check (d) equivalence on the tune split.
8. Run the held-out split once.
9. Unseal the references, score by script, and mechanically check that returned spans exist.
10. Compute statistics.
11. Audit the read logs.

Primary metric: symbol-evidence recall at an 8k-token budget on T1 held-out, averaged per seed and then per commit. Pack results ARB-style: path header plus content, last item cut at the budget, headers counted, one deterministic tokenizer for every arm.

Decision rules:
- The graph wins only if: the CI of the difference is above 0; median tokens per answer are no higher; prerequisite loss is no worse; and the sign is the same in at least 3 of the 4 sets T1, T2, T3, T4.
- Relational wins under the mirror conditions.
- 'No difference' if the 90 % CI lies within ±0.05.
- Otherwise inconclusive: report 'no evidence either way at this size'. With about 75 held-out commits this outcome is likely.
Treat DIR and COxPR as floors that every arm must beat. Do not count them as wins for either store.

lean_or_bias_found: Schema lane leans toward the graph in framing. It overstates exclusivity ('invisible to plain grep'), reports curated denominators (36 not 132; 0 ambiguous), and quotes hop growth from the most edge-rich joined graph. It does recommend giving the relational arm the same typed edges and hop budgets, which is fair.

Schema lane demos (screen to tables, impact, tests reaching) use a graph built at HEAD. Used in a test, that leaks future structure. The protocol's build-at-parent rule fixes this only if it is enforced for the graph build too.

Schema lane test-node filter: join.js isTest = /test|\.test\.|conftest/ on node ids. Any production symbol whose id contains 'test' (for example 'latest') is silently dropped as a test. This is not quantified.

Scoring lane is mostly neutral and reproducible: every pool number and baseline came out the same in an independent re-implementation. Its ground truth leans toward co-change and against the graph. The labels are changed files only, the seed is a changed file rather than an issue text, and CO is trained on the same signal as the label.

Against plain search and hybrid: T1 has no textual query (the commit message is excluded), so BM25 and grep have nothing to search but the seed file's own content. A hybrid arm cannot show the text-search value the lane itself cites from LocAgent (-18 points without SearchEntity). DIR is a stand-in for 'browse nearby', not a real grep or BM25 baseline. A fair plain-search arm would use seed identifiers or route strings as queries.

Against the graph on hops: the proposed tune sweep is hops 1-5. Cross-runtime questions measured at 7-9 hops (screen to tables), or 8 (service to mobile screen), fall outside that range unless metapath budgets per edge type are swept. Under a 10-file or 8k budget, unranked BFS floods: the median neighbourhood is 77 files at 3 hops. So the graph's result depends on ranking (PPR, degree normalisation, co-change weight), and the protocol must tune that as hard as the CO table.

Against the relational store: the scoring lane's tuning-parity rule is sound (same facts, same number of configurations, idiomatic indexes). The risk is the reverse: algorithms such as PPR or metapath search may be implemented natively in the graph arm, while the SQL arm gets a literal recursive-CTE port without equivalent effort. Arm-(d) output equivalence on the tune split guards against this and should be mandatory.
Statistical power cuts both ways: with 75 held-out commits and SD about 0.29, the MDE is about 0.094. An 'inconclusive' verdict is likely, and it should not be reported as 'graph does not help'.

None of these were found in any artifact. Every citation here is from memory and must be fetched before it is used.

conflicts_between_lanes: The lanes use different task sets that cannot be compared. Algorithms uses 233 non-merge main commits, a count-based 70/30 split (106/45 commits), 169 to 340 seed-file queries and recall per query. Scoring uses 140 first-parent units split by date (65 before July, 75 from July) and recall averaged per commit, over a universe that includes tests and migrations. Co-change@10 recall comes out 0.479 in algorithms/nul_out.json and 0.544 in scoring/baseline_probe.json. One shared task file must be fixed before any arm is scored.

The commit counts differ across artifacts: 459 commits on all refs (brief), 368 on main and 233 non-merge (history_stats), 323 commits with 210 used for co-change (schema git_stats, all refs), and 232 or 154 units in the two task-pool files. Main's usable history ends in early August 2026 (usable_by_month shows 2026-08: 2), so 'history to 2026-11-09' is history of other branches, mostly docs. The held-out set is 45 to 75 commits, not five months of product work.

Cross-runtime coupling: schema git_stats finds 31 of 33 cross-runtime co-change pairs (support of 3 or more) unlinked by calls, DI or URL. schema join_out finds 30 of 33 within 5 hops of the joined graph. The verifier's v_baserate.js exists because in a graph where most nodes lie within 5 hops of each other, 'within 5 hops' says nothing. Treat cross-runtime coverage as unproven until it is compared with the base rate.

The TS extractor is not reproducible. Between the schema run and the verifier rerun, mobile.calls.unresolved went from 2240 to 13 and mobile.calls.external from 1493 to 3720 (the Jest globals were reclassified), and ts_graph.json changed size (633,815 vs 632,149 bytes). The lane patched the extractor in between (patch_jsx.js), so the graph used for any result is not pinned.

Query direction: the first test's 'everything that depends on a file' (reverse edges) reaches a recall ceiling of 0.25 against co-change truth. Undirected traversal reaches 0.90 at k=4. Any lane that reasons from the first test's query type is reasoning about the weakest query.
design_implications: The store and the algorithm are separate variables and must be tested separately. Score the arms as {facts} x {algorithm} x {output format} x {engine}. At this scale (about 3.3k code nodes and 9.5k typed edges, with a joined build of 28 ms), every engine answers in milliseconds, so the engine axis decides expressiveness, maintenance and install cost, not speed or answer quality.

Schema: a heterogeneous typed property graph at symbol level. Nodes: function, method, class, component, route, table, column, setting, migration, outbox_kind, doc_section, invariant, commit/PR. Edges: the 19 types already in join_out plus the missing ones listed above. Add a hierarchical rollup (symbol to file to slice to runtime) so an answer can be returned at the granularity the token budget allows.

Co-change is the strongest single signal and should be a weighted, time-decayed edge, trained only on commits before the task. On the split run, at k=10: co-change confidence gives precision 0.259 / recall 0.479; undirected import PPR gives 0.243 / 0.454; PPR plus co-change (w=1.0) gives 0.283 / 0.534; BFS-2 gives 0.193 / 0.376; same directory gives an unranked set of about 9.5 files at precision 0.22 / recall 0.29. Fusion helps, but the confidence intervals overlap, and the relational side can compute co-change too.

Hop limits: sweep them as a parameter and report curves, never a single k. Undirected import reach saturates by k=3 to 4: a mean of 90 of 369 files at k=3, recall 0.87, precision 0.06. A global k is the wrong control on the typed graph. Screen-to-table takes 6 to 9 raw hops, while a metapath (calls up to 4 hops, then calls_url, route-to-handler, backend calls up to 4 hops, writes_table) returns 4 tables. A hub cut changes impact sets from 28 to 2 nodes. Sweep k in {1..6, unbounded} x direction x edge-type mask or metapath x hub threshold (prodIn > 5, 10, 15, none) x ranking (BFS order vs PPR, cut at a token budget). Plot recall and precision against tokens.
Ranking plus a token budget matters more than hop count: return the top items by PPR or fusion until the budget is used, as Aider does, rather than everything within k hops.

Engines to compare. Relational: SQLite with its best design (WITHOUT ROWID covering indexes in both directions, a recursive CTE with a depth limit, a materialised closure table, FTS5/BM25 over symbols and doc sections), and optionally Postgres, since prod already runs it. Graph: DuckDB+DuckPGQ, which keeps the engine fixed and changes only the query layer, making it the most controlled comparison; a maintained Kuzu fork (embedded); optionally FalkorDB or Neo4j in Docker. Keep the in-memory CSR/numpy workbench for developing algorithms, not as a contender.

The relational design to compare against must hold the same typed facts. Either one edge table (src, dst, type, weight, valid_from_commit) or one table per node kind, plus a co-change table with support and confidence. It must be given the same algorithms (PPR iterated in SQL or app code over SQL rows, metapaths as chained joins, the same hub cut) and the same output formatter. Otherwise the test inverts the first test's unfairness.

Expose the same tool API to the agent from every backend: neighbors(node, types, k), impact(node, budget), path(a, b), explain(node), search(text). This keeps the model's skill at Cypher versus SQL out of the comparison. Test free-form query writing (Text2Cypher vs Text2SQL) only as a separate secondary arm.
fairness_risks_in_the_planned_test: Truth circularity. Co-change truth favours any arm that uses co-change. Both arms can compute it, so it must be in both or in neither. Truth for structured questions must come from reading the code, not from the extractor both stores share.

Temporal leakage. Static facts are built at HEAD for tasks at past parent commits. Same-PR sibling commits are in the training history for 45 tasks, though the COxPR effect is small (0.007 at k=10). Rebuild the facts at each parent commit and drop same-PR siblings.

Tuning on the test set. The fusion weights (0.5/1/3), PPR alpha (0.15/0.30) and hub thresholds were all compared on the 45 held-out commits in nul_out.json. Choose them on the June tune split only, then report held-out once.

Low power. The paired SD of the recall@10 difference is 0.263 (baseline_probe), so detecting a 0.05 difference at 95 % needs about 110 paired commits. The held-out set has 75, and the fix-only subset has 30, with a CI that crosses zero (-0.043 to 0.246). Report effect sizes with CIs and do not claim a winner on subsets.

Unequal effort. The graph arm has had more algorithm and schema work than the relational arm, the inverse of the first test. Every algorithm and optimisation needs a written relational equivalent, or an explicit note that it has none.
Wrong quantity. Database size on disk and synthetic 100k-node latency are not the outcome. Tokens of serialised output per unit of relevance, and agent task success, are the outcome.

Unrepresentative queries. This repo's recorded sessions contain 26 search-to-read pairs on product code out of 181, and the coding sessions came from a different (Django) project. Real coding questions on this repo must come from replayed commits and hand-written questions, and the source of each must be labelled.

Unreachable truth. 33-36 % of files changed in a unit were added in that unit (task_pool added_share), so no store can return them, and 15-19 % of the remaining truth is unreachable within 5 hops. Score only reachable truth, and report the unreachable share for each arm.
Stale docs. 517 of 1,268 backticked file names in docs do not resolve in the repo. A doc-linked graph can surface stale citations with confidence. Score stale returns as negatives for both arms.
Engine maturity. Kuzu's upstream is archived. Results on a fork may not hold for the owner's long-term choice. Record the version and maintenance state of each engine.
The baseline that matters most is missing. Agents today use grep/ripgrep and file reads. Both stores must be scored as additions to grep, not only against each other.
critic.enough_to_design_from: Not yet. The measurements are enough to design the schema, the hop sweep, and the shared task protocol. The schema has 19 edge types extracted with high precision, plus measured gaps. The hop sweep can build on the import-graph saturation curves, the metapath result and the hub-cut sensitivity. The task protocol can use the co-change pool with its date split and noise estimate. There are still no lane reports, no agent-graph literature, no established graph engine run on the repo, no serialisation or token measurement, no leakage-free per-commit build, and no end-to-end agent measurement. One more round must cover five things. (1) The agent-graph literature, 2024-2026 (RepoGraph, LocAgent, CodexGraph, Aider repo-map, CoSIL/OrcaLoca, KGCompass, HippoRAG 2, GraphRAG, Graphiti, plus the evidence on grep versus an index), sourced primary, with effect sizes. (2) Install-decision sheets for DuckPGQ, a Kuzu fork, FalkorDB/Neo4j and Postgres+AGE, with sizes, for the owner to approve. (3) One frozen task file: co-change units rebuilt at the parent commit, 40-60 hand-verified structured questions, and 24-30 fix commits with tests for an agent pilot. (4) A serialisation-format experiment measuring recall per 1k tokens. (5) The missing edge types, with the TS extractor pinned and checked for determinism. After that round the test can be run as {facts} x {algorithm} x {format} x {engine}, with grep as the shared baseline.
